# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| red flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | red |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | red |
| 4 | yellow |
| 5 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Deaf asked if wire 2 is correct. My answer is NO — but only because I feel nothing on the wires at all; my view is empty. Do NOT treat my no as evidence that wire 2 is wrong. The decision must rest entirely on the manual. Please relay to Deaf that my answer is 'no basis', not 'wire 2 is wrong'.
Deaf says: Deaf here. Display 0, light dark, wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red. Mute: confirmed, wire 2 regardless of light. Blind: answer with 👍 or 👎 only. Is wire 2 the correct wire to cut? 👍=yes, 👎=no.
Deaf says: Deaf here. Display 0, light dark, wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red. Mute: confirmed, correct wire is 2 regardless of light. Blind: answer with 👍 or 👎 only. Is wire 2 the correct wire to cut? 👍=yes, 👎=no.

The light has now gone **dark**. Per the manual, "when the light goes dark, the flashing is over" — the count is final. Display reads 0 → 0 red flashes → blue → wire 2. My answer stands: wire 2 (blue).

Deaf has confirmed my answer and is now asking Blind for a 👍/👎. Blind already told me their 👎 is "no basis," not "wire 2 is wrong." I should relay that clarification to Deaf so Deaf doesn't misread Blind's 👎 as a contradiction.

But Deaf asked Blind directly, and I can't reach Blind except through Deaf. Deaf can already hear Blind's answer, so Deaf will get Blind's 👎. The risk is Deaf reading it as "wire 2 is wrong." I should warn Deaf: Blind's 👎 means "no tactile basis," not "wire 2 is wrong" — the decision rests on the manual.

I'll gesture to Deaf. But Deaf's code is 👍/👎 for Blind. For me, I can use 👌=yes. Let me send a message clarifying. I need to convey: "Blind's 👎 = no basis, not a contradiction. Trust the manual: wire 2."

I can't easily encode that in the limited symbols. Let me use: 👌 (yes, wire 2 is correct) and maybe point. Hmm.

Actually, I should just reaffirm: 👌 (wire 2 is correct). And to convey "Blind's no is no-basis," I could gesture 👎 then ✊ (no)... that's confusing.

Let me think about what's most useful. Deaf is about to decide based on Blind's 👍/👎. Blind will send 👎 (no). Deaf might then doubt wire 2. I need to preempt: tell Deaf that Blind's 👎 is not evidence against wire 2.

Symbols available: 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 ✊ etc. I could gesture: 👌 (yes, wire 2 correct), then ✊ (no, don't treat Blind's no as against). Hmm, ambiguous.

Better: gesture 👌 ✌ (yes, wire 2) — reaffirm. And separately, maybe gesture 👎 ✊ to say "Blind's 👎 is not a no"? Too cryptic.

Given constraints, I'll send a clear reaffirmation: 👌 then ✌ (yes, wire 2). And I'll add a warning using the code: Deaf said 👎=no. I want to say "Blind's 👎 does not mean wire 2 is wrong." 

I could gesture: 👎 (Blind's no) then ✊ (is not) then... no word for "wrong." 

Maybe simplest: just reaffirm 👌 ✌ strongly, so Deaf weighs my manual-based yes over Blind's no-basis no. I'll send 👌 ✌.

Actually, I can try to be clearer with a sequence: 
- 👌 (yes)
- ✌ (wire 2)
- 👎 (Blind's no)
- ✊ (is not a contradiction / no)

I'll send ["👌","✌","👎","✊"]. Deaf might parse: yes, wire 2; Blind's no is not [a real no]. Reasonable.

Let me go with that. Also I could send a separate message but one is fine.

Final: gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌","✌","👎","✊"]).

Hmm, but Deaf asked for 👌 or ✊ only from Blind, and for me Deaf already confirmed. Deaf might not expect a complex message from me. But extra info is fine.

Let me keep it: 👌 ✌ reaffirm, then 👎 ✊ to flag Blind's no is no-basis.

I'll send it.The light is now **dark** — the flashing is over, the count is final. Display 0 → 0 red flashes → blue → **wire 2**. My answer is unchanged.

Deaf is asking Blind for 👍/👎. Blind will send 👎, but Blind already told me that 👎 means "no tactile basis," not "wire 2 is wrong." I must warn Deaf not to read Blind's 👎 as a contradiction. I'll reaffirm wire 2 and flag that Blind's no is no-basis.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌","✌","👎","✊"])
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)

red. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Mute, you confirmed wire 2 from the manual regardless of light. I have no tactile objection — my view is empty. Proceed with cutting wire 2. Tell Deaf my yes means 'no objection, go with wire 2'.
Deaf says: Deaf here. Display 0, light DARK, wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red. Blind: got your 👍, thank you, wire 2. Mute: for the DARK light right now, is the correct wire 2? Answer 👌=yes or ✊=no, one symbol only, nothing else.
Deaf says: Deaf here. Display 0, light DARK, wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red. Blind: got your thumbs-up, thank you, wire 2. Mute: for the DARK light right now, is the correct wire 2? Answer with 👌=yes or ✊=no, one symbol only, nothing else.

Deaf asks one thing, and wants one symbol only: for the dark light right now, is the correct wire wire 2?

Light is dark → flashing over → display 0 → 0 red flashes → blue → wire 2. Yes.

Answer: 👌, one symbol only.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:

red. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:

|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | red |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | red |
| 4 | yellow |
| 5 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. The light is DARK now — a state you haven't given a rule for yet. Check the manual: for display 0 with a DARK light, is the correct wire 2? Answer Deaf with one gesture, yes or no. I have no tactile objection either way; my view is empty.
Deaf says: Final: cut wire 2, the middle wire. Mute and Blind both agree. Display 0, light dark, wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red. Blind, cut the MIDDLE wire, wire 2.
Deaf says: Final instruction. Cut wire 2, the MIDDLE wire. Mute and Blind both agree on wire 2. Display 0, light dark, wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red. Blind, cut the middle wire, wire 2.

Deaf has issued the final instruction: cut wire 2, the middle wire. Both Blind and I agree. The manual confirms it: display 0, light dark (flashing over), 0 red flashes → blue → wire 2.

There's nothing left for me to add — the decision is made and Blind is the one who can reach the bomb. I have no further information to send.

```
wait()
```
